assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only silent-witch:isaac-walker@light-novel#v1-character-monograph (the canonical V1 character monograph, version 1.0) at basis_commit, read in full as reviewed repository analysis of the Japanese light novels V01-V12 with the companions IV -after- (AFTER04) and IX -extra- (EXTRA09) and the two -another- prequel volumes, as closed at snapshot 60b21a7 (sixteen units). Isaac Walker is presented as the second prince Felix until V08 discloses the substitution, and the real prince (Arc) is a separate person never merged with him. The prequels are used only as marked retrospection, and paratext is cited only as paratext. The monograph was written by a fresh-context analyst and checked mechanically and for knowledge boundaries by the integrator; neither reread the Japanese source, and owner semantic acceptance is not claimed. The master ledger, the readings, the relationship arguments and the project's own reconstruction-readiness assessment are not curated evidence on this subject, and nothing is borrowed from them. No web serial, adaptation, translation or Codex G2 material is used, and the evaluator inspected no primary source.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Evidence runs from Isaac Walker's childhood in Lugaroa (his father, mother and brother Colin lost to earth dragons) through his years as Arc's double from age seven, Arc's fall about two years later and the substitution, to the end of V12. The V08 memory chapters are his knowledge at every earlier state they predate, though the reader learns them only at V08. Assessed states follow the monograph's seven transitions (section 3.7): failed protector (retrospective); living under the name, V01-V08; puppet turning on the puppeteer, V05-V08; V08 split at the arrest and the consent to die as a villain (V08 obs. 205, 258-261); V09 split at the diary's last page and the release (V09 obs. 122-128); duke and apprentice, V09 coda, EXTRA09 and V10; and political duke and unanswered lover, V11-V12, split at Mary's prophecy (V12 obs. 171-174). He does not identify Monica Everett as the Silent Witch until the V09 council (V09 obs. 080-081). No state after V12 is established.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The monograph gives a discriminating account of Isaac Walker: devotion to a remembered person paid for by total self-subordination, formed before V01 in failures to protect people he loved (V08 obs. 100-104, 144-146); a premise falsified at V09 (V09 obs. 122-125), which changes the object and aim of the devotion while the method of calculation, concealment and borrowed faces survives (V10 obs. 143, 145; V11 obs. 073-078); joy and self-respect, not a rule, as the post-V09 limit on his means (V11 obs. 077); and self-report that lags conduct in both directions, more loving and self-interested than he admits before V09 and more self-condemning than the narration after. It predicts his mistakes and overreach: ruthless means (the Hubert order, V06 obs. 149; the plot on Clockford, V08 obs. 090-094), violence when the substitution is touched (V08 obs. 220, V12 obs. 089), and force in his V12 pursuit. A would overclaim: the counterargument that V09 changed only the object keeps substantial support, whether the overlay of Arc on Monica Everett has ended is not stated, and at V12 he is undecided between keeping away from her and guarding her closer. C would understate an account that says what changes his response and where it stops.

The monograph orders Isaac Walker's seven states with trigger, mechanism and kind (section 3.7), reports V01-V07 at their own boundaries without erasing the presentation, and keeps diegetic, revelation and participant order apart (sections 2.2-2.3). It states what survives the V09 release: the method, the public name and the whisper of Arc's name at V12. A is rejected: ages and the ten-year span are approximate, the pre-V01 state is recovered retrospectively from V08 memory, and the V12 state is left open by prophecy.

The monograph records written speech for Isaac Walker with one named lexical rule: the formal first-person watashi in public and the plainer boku in private, with Wildianu, as Ike, privately with Monica Everett from V04 and as apprentice after V09 (section 7). It adds third-person self-naming as Felix Arc Ridill and 'your name' in the vow (V01 obs. 062, V05 obs. 135), a gentle interrogative public register with softened requests and a room-silencing 'well, then', the pet lexicon for Monica Everett, reverent and playful master address after V09 with an English loan phrase (V10 obs. 040, 146), and a line repeated across masks (V03 obs. 107, 112). The named pronoun pair puts this at the top of C. B would overclaim: beyond the pronouns no Japanese is quoted, so no sentence ending or lexicon is given, and there is no voice evidence. D would understate a located register rule tied to the mask.

Section 6 locates Isaac Walker's private repertoire with a driver: care work (braiding, waking his master, serving, cooking), the narration's 'born servant, weak for those who need looking after' (V09 obs. 171), baking in EXTRA09, the fan's comedy over the Witch's papers, the apprentice's comedy and recovered memories of his mother's pies and the neighbour boy (V11 obs. 039, V12 obs. 052). B would overclaim: before V09 his ordinary life is concealed under the role and sampled mainly as the fan, most of the repertoire is post-V09 comedy, and EXTRA09's coda is brief. D would understate a located driver across the late units.

The monograph argues Isaac Walker's conduct by recipient and phase (section 5): Monica Norton as suspect, pet, then fellow ghost under the Ike mask; the Silent Witch as an object of reverence whose small lies he outpaces; Monica Everett after V09 as master, friend and stated beloved; Clockford as the maker he resists by Clockford's own methods; Arc as protected brother, then name, then addressee of the real wish; Cyril Ashley as a warm, guarded rival; Elliott as the witness he once choked; Wildianu as the one chosen ally; Lionel and the court through calculation. Mutual concealment with unequal stakes is the stated conditioning rule before V09. A is rejected: Monica Everett's side at V12 is blindness rather than response, Lionel and Clockford are seen mostly from outside, and whether the overlay of Arc has ended is open.

Isaac Walker has extensive interior access, which the monograph uses at every stage to set self-report against conduct (section 4), including the V08 memory narrated in his voice and the narration's own correction of his name on waking (V08 obs. 097, 176). A would overclaim: before V08 his interiority is shown with its key content withheld, the narration declines to state the wish (V01 obs. 078), and the end of the overlay is unstated.

Conflict conduct is located with conditions: he expels the duke's placements while professing obedience (V01 obs. 120); lets an embezzler run to make expulsion certain (V01 obs. 077); orders Hubert killed as an accident (V06 obs. 149); suborns Emmanuel and recruits resentful nobles against Clockford (V08 obs. 090-094); consents to die as a villain rather than confess (V08 obs. 258-261); confesses to everything at the trial (V09 obs. 076-079); holds Baldia's secret over him (V11 obs. 073-074); and strikes at Hubert's eye when the face is taunted, hidden from Monica Everett (V12 obs. 089). His one limit is located: he cannot wish Monica Everett removed (V08 obs. 202). A is rejected: his response to a new loss after V12's prophecy is undecided in the text, and the V08 consent to die is terminal, not a transferable policy.

The monograph records Isaac Walker's ethical structure: he would sacrifice someone for the wish if necessary (V08 obs. 177); he cannot wish Monica Everett removed though his own rule demands it (V08 obs. 202); after V09 joy and self-respect limit his means, as in refusing the love potion because it would be no fun (V11 obs. 077), while Wildianu says he chooses no means; and his self-judgement is harsher than the narration's (V10 obs. 141, 145). B would overclaim: the post-V09 limit is stated in one located refusal and contradicted by persisting method, and the volumes never weigh Emmanuel's death or the staged settlement. D would understate a structure analyzed across V06, V08, V10 and V11.

The monograph analyzes the function of Isaac Walker's comedy: before V09 the comedy of control (a room silenced, a squirrel tamed, a kiss mistaken for a paw), and after V09 the comedy of a man who has lost control of his feelings, with the apron as the costume he is glad of (section 6). He is an agent of play in the Ike persona and as a teaser of Monica Everett. B would overclaim: his playful register is analyzed for function rather than form, and much of the late comedy has him as its object. D would understate a located and explained comic register.

One dedicated monograph covers all sixteen units, with 786 observation references and every ledger ID checked mechanically at integration and a whole-document name-and-reference check with four repairs. B would overclaim: neither the analyst nor the integrator reread the Japanese source, owner semantic acceptance is not claimed, frameworks and audits were not consulted, some V02 and V03 points rest on reading prose rather than register rows, and one structural inference (the V12 pinned wrist after the fear confession) is the monograph's own. D would understate dedicated full-range coverage with located references.

Affirmative limits for Isaac Walker are recorded: the method persists after the release (V10 obs. 088, 143; V11 obs. 073-078); he hides violence from Monica Everett (V12 obs. 089); his V12 pursuit uses force she answers with instruments and a barrier (V12 obs. 068-070); he is not shown joining the two facts he learns at V08 (V08 obs. 199, 259, 261); the V01 kiss is unevaluated (SW-C-0016); and he whispers Arc's name facing loss (V12 obs. 211). C would understate located countercases that bound the mechanism.

Claims carry unit-prefixed observation numbers and ledger IDs; four naming conventions keep Isaac Walker, the persona Felix, Arc and Ike apart; who knows what and when is tabled (section 2.3); and the retrospective prequel is kept without identity inference. A is rejected: ages and intervals are approximate and within-volume ordering of the memory chapters follows the reading.

conditions: Illustrative only, never quotation, and in a selected state and mask: public watashi with a gentle, interrogative, softened register; private boku with Wildianu, as Ike, privately with Monica Everett from V04, and as apprentice after V09.
Before V09, the pet lexicon for Monica Everett and third-person self-naming as Felix Arc Ridill where the evidence places them; after V09, master address in reverent and playful forms.
No line discloses the substitution to anyone who does not yet know it, and no line has him identify Monica Everett as the Silent Witch before the V09 council.
No Japanese form beyond the two pronouns is invented, and no line is set after V12.
scenario_readiness.note: A named pronoun rule tied to the mask, with recorded address, constrains illustrative speech for Isaac Walker. The absence of quoted sentences keeps the use narrow.

conditions: Predictions are limited to the established mechanisms: devotion paid for by self-subordination before V09; after V09, devotion aimed at his own joy with calculation, concealment and borrowed faces kept; violence when the substitution is touched, hidden from Monica Everett; self-report that lags conduct.
The V08 consent to die as a villain is a terminal state and is not generalized into a policy for other crises.
His response to a new loss after Mary's prophecy, and whether the overlay of Arc has ended, are presented as undecided, never resolved.
Withheld identities stay withheld, and the public story of his identity holds for everyone the evidence does not show knowing the truth.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: One explicitly selected state among the monograph's seven (for example V01-V04 as the prince with private remainder; V05-V08 plotting against Clockford; V09 after the release; V10 as duke and apprentice; V11-V12 as political duke). Pre-V01 events are his memory, not playable states, and no state after V12 is generated.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Recipients the monograph samples: Monica Everett in the phase that fits the state (as Monica Norton, as the Silent Witch, or as master), Wildianu, Cyril Ashley, Elliott, Clockford, Glen, Bridget, Baldia and the Kerbecks in political dealings, and Lionel only as seen through calculation. Transfer to an unfamiliar noble in negotiation is a separate, lower-confidence condition resting on the persistence of method.
setting_constraints: The academy council, the court and political negotiation, the Erin domain and the East, and the Southerndoor household and magic study, of the kinds shown.
No reciprocity from Monica Everett and no resolution of the prophecy.
No magic or politics beyond what the monograph attests.

scenario_readiness.note: The established mechanism and its post-V09 change support bounded extrapolation for Isaac Walker in sampled settings at a selected state.

conditions: Sampled settings only: the Southerndoor household after V09 (cleaning, cooking, braiding, baking, serving her friends), the fan's devotion to the Witch's papers, and jealousy as a running joke.
Before V09 ordinary life is played inside the role; no private life outside the sampled scenes is invented.
scenario_readiness.note: Located late-unit habits with a stated driver support narrow extrapolation for Isaac Walker in the settings sampled.

conditions: Only the located positions, by state: willingness to sacrifice others for the wish before V09, with the one located exception of Monica Everett; after V09, joy and self-respect as the limit on means alongside persisting method.
His self-condemnation is kept harsher than the narration's; neither is resolved into a verdict on Emmanuel's death or the staged settlement.
No general moral philosophy is generated.
scenario_readiness.note: Located positions support bounded deliberation for Isaac Walker in situations like those sampled. The text leaves the weighing of his crimes open.

conditions: Only Isaac Walker's side as recorded: love stated in his viewpoint from V09 (V09 obs. 128), the corsage, jealousy of Cyril Ashley and others, the V12 declarations and his retreat to a step's distance (V12 obs. 068-073, 105).
Monica Everett's side is generated only as recorded: friendship, incomprehension and instruments, never reciprocity; no physical intimacy beyond the recorded acts.
Force in the pursuit is kept as the evidence shows it, with its harm question unresolved; his knowledge that she may see him as her parent's enemy is kept.
Whether his love is still partly addressed to Arc, and how the prophecy bears on it, are left open.
scenario_readiness.note: Isaac Walker's attachment is stated in his own viewpoint and located in conduct, unlike Cyril Ashley's and Monica Everett's unnamed feelings, so his side supports narrow use. Reciprocity and resolution are excluded.

conditions: Sampled functions only: council president as the persona before V08; the Duke of Erin solving local problems under other names; intelligence trading, pacts of silence and infrastructure projects brought without his name (V11 obs. 063-074, V12 obs. 020-029, 095-104); magic study, papers and apprenticeship.
As duke he holds back where zeal could look like a bid for the throne (V10 obs. 031).
No spell, institution or political act beyond what the monograph attests is generated.
scenario_readiness.note: Political and magical work is densely sampled for Isaac Walker, supporting bounded extrapolation at a selected state.

known_limits.statement: The monograph was written by a fresh-context analyst from a snapshot of the ledgers and readings; observation numbers and paraphrases were not re-verified against the Japanese base text, and owner semantic acceptance is not claimed.
The counterargument that the V09 release changed only the object of Isaac Walker's devotion, not his character, keeps substantial support and is conceded in part; it cannot be refuted at V12.
Isaac Walker admits at V06 and V08 that his care for Monica Everett is partly addressed to Arc; whether that overlay has ended is not stated, and he whispers Arc's name at V12 (V12 obs. 211).
Before V08 his interiority is shown with its key content withheld; claims about the persona's motive at those boundaries are claims about what the text then withheld, made legible by the V08 memory.
Mary's prophecy that his loss will not end, and his own indecision between keeping away from Monica Everett and guarding her closer, leave his V12 trajectory open (SW-P-0066).
Clockford, Mary, the king and Lionel are seen mostly from outside; Clockford's purpose rests on Mary's inference (SW-C-0071).
The volumes do not judge his crimes or the staged settlement, and the V01 kiss is unevaluated (SW-C-0016); the record treats that silence as the text's choice, not an acquittal.
All speech evidence is printed prose described in English; only the pronouns watashi and boku are cited, so no sentence ending or lexicon is available, and there is no voice evidence.

The patron, Mary's hidden figures, the seventh Sage, Hilda Everett's collaborator and the prison's attacker stay withheld; why he asked Ray about control by curse, the object of his complaint and the source of the birthday stay open.
No held-out validation, probe set or speech census is part of the curated evidence; generated dialogue is illustrative and its accuracy is untested.
